tasks.title: JSON in SQL: extract a field
tasks.statement: In the table events(id, payload), payload is JSON. Output user and amount for events of type 'buy' (columns: user, amount), in ascending id order.
tasks.hint: The ->> operator extracts a value by path: payload ->> '$.user'; or json_extract(payload, '$.user').
tasks.starter:
-- user and amount of purchases
SELECT

tasks.title: JSON array into rows
tasks.statement: Count how many times each tag occurs across all events (the tags array in payload). Columns: tag, n; most frequent first, ties by alphabet.
tasks.hint: json_each(payload, '$.tags') expands an array into rows; the value is in the value column.

tasks.title: Index on a JSON field
tasks.statement: The query WHERE payload ->> '$.user' = 'anna' scans the table. Create an expression index so that it becomes an index search.
tasks.hint: An expression index: ON events ((payload ->> '$.user')) — the expression in parentheses must match the query.
tasks.starter:
-- index on the user field inside JSON
CREATE INDEX

tasks.title: Build documents from tables
tasks.statement: For each customer build a document: a JSON object with the fields id, name and orders — an array of their order numbers in ascending order. Columns: doc (JSON text); ordered by customer id; customers without orders are needed too (orders is an empty array).
tasks.hint: json_object(...) builds an object, json_group_array(...) an array; wrap the nested array in json() so it does not become a string.
tasks.starter:
-- one JSON document per customer
SELECT

tasks.title: Graph in SQL: friends of friends
tasks.statement: friends(a, b) is friendship in both directions (stored as a pair of rows). Output Anna's friends of friends — those who are not Anna herself and not her direct friends (column name, in alphabetical order).
tasks.hint: Two self-joins: a friend (f1) and their friend (f2); exclude Anna herself and her direct friends.

tasks.title: Key-value with time to live
tasks.statement: Operations: ["set", t, key, value, ttl] (ttl is a number of seconds or None) and ["get", t, key], where t is a point in time. A record lives until t + ttl, exclusive: at the moment t + ttl it is already gone. Write kv_run(ops): a list of the results of all gets in execution order (the value or None).
tasks.hint: Store the value together with its expiry time; get returns it only if t is less than that time.

tasks.title: Atomic counters
tasks.statement: Operations on counters: ["incr", key, delta] and ["decr", key, delta]; a missing key counts as zero. Write counters(ops): a dictionary of the final values.
tasks.hint: c.get(key, 0) gives zero for a new key; decr is adding a negative delta.

tasks.title: Composite keys
tasks.statement: A key is built from parts joined by a colon. So that a colon and a percent sign inside a part do not break parsing, they are escaped: «%» → «%25», «:» → «%3A» (percent first). Write make_key(parts): a list of parts (strings or numbers) is turned into a key; an empty list gives an empty string.
tasks.hint: Escape each part (first %, then :), then join them with a colon.

tasks.title: Conditions on document fields
tasks.statement: A document is a nested dictionary. A query is a dictionary of "dotted path → condition". A condition is a value (equality) or a dictionary with a single operator: {"$gt": x}, {"$lt": x}, {"$in": [..]}. Write doc_match(doc, query): True if the document satisfies all conditions; a missing field fails the condition.
tasks.hint: Descend along the path parts; for dictionary conditions, one of the three operations; no field means False immediately.

tasks.title: Search in a collection
tasks.statement: A collection is a list of documents with a string field "id". A query is a dictionary of "top-level field → value or {"$gt": x}". Write find_ids(docs, query): a sorted list of ids of matching documents (a document matches if, for every field of the query, the field exists and the condition holds).
tasks.hint: For each document, check all fields of the query; sort the result.

tasks.title: Denormalization: embed the author
tasks.statement: Orders are a list of dictionaries with a user_id field, users are a dictionary of "id (string) → {"name": …}". Write embed_users(orders, users): a new list of orders in which the user_id field is replaced with a user field — a copy of the user's dictionary (None if there is no such user). Keep the other fields of the order.
tasks.hint: Copy the order fields without user_id and add user from the dictionary by the key str(user_id).

tasks.title: Partition key → node
tasks.statement: The node for a key is defined as (sum of the character codes of the key) % nodes. Write partition_keys(keys, nodes): a dictionary of "node number (string) → sorted list of keys" only for nodes that have keys.
tasks.hint: Compute the hash by the rule, group, and sort inside the groups; the dictionary keys are strings.

tasks.title: Range on the clustering key
tasks.statement: Rows are a list of [partition, clustering (a number), value] in arbitrary order. Write slice_rows(rows, partition, start, end): the values of the partition with clustering start ≤ c < end, ordered by c.
tasks.hint: Select the right partition and range, sort the pairs by clustering.

tasks.title: Friends of friends in a graph
tasks.statement: A graph is a dictionary of "name → list of friends" (friendship is symmetric, but you do not need to check that). Write friends_of_friends(graph, person): a sorted list of people who are friends of friends of person, but not person themselves and not their direct friends.
tasks.hint: Collect the set of friends of friends and subtract the direct friends and the person themselves.

tasks.title: Shortest path in a graph
tasks.statement: Write shortest_path(graph, a, b): the number of edges in the shortest path between a and b using breadth-first search (the graph is a dictionary of "node → list of neighbors"); if there is no path, -1; for a == b, 0.
tasks.hint: Breadth-first traversal by layers: each layer is one step farther; when b is found, return the layer number.

tasks.title: Inverted index
tasks.statement: Documents are a dictionary of "id (string) → text". Words are consecutive letters and digits, case does not matter. Write build_index(docs): a dictionary of "word → sorted list of ids of documents containing it" (no repeats).
tasks.hint: Split the text into words with a regular expression, make a set of the document's words, and add the id to each word's list.

tasks.title: Search by all words
tasks.statement: The index is a dictionary of "word → list of ids". Write search_all(index, query): a sorted list of ids of documents that contain ALL the words of the query (the query is a string, words are separated by spaces, case does not matter). An empty query gives an empty list.
tasks.hint: Intersect the sets of ids for each word of the query; a missing word gives an empty set.

tasks.title: Ranking by word frequency
tasks.statement: Documents are a dictionary of "id → text". A document's score is the sum, over the query words, of the number of occurrences of the word in the document (case does not matter). Write rank(docs, query): a list of ids with a positive score, in descending order of score, ties by ascending id.
tasks.hint: The score is the sum of words.count(word) over the query words; sort by the pair (−score, id).

tasks.title: Flat document paths
tasks.statement: For indexing, a nested document is turned into a flat dictionary of "dotted path → value". Write flatten_doc(doc): leaves (non-dictionaries) go into the result, nested dictionaries are expanded recursively; treat lists as leaves.
tasks.hint: Recursion with an accumulated prefix: the top-level key + '.' + the nested keys.

tasks.title: Validate a document against a schema
tasks.statement: A schema is a dictionary of "field → type" with the types 'str', 'int' or 'bool'; all fields are required. Write validate(doc, schema): a sorted list of errors — "missing:field" for a missing field and "type:field" for a wrong type (bool does not count as int).
tasks.hint: For each field of the schema: absent — missing, wrong type — type; bool is a subclass of int, so it must be excluded manually.
